extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) that requires models to read and reason about text in images to answer questions. The dataset contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images where answering questions necessitates understanding embedded text in the images. Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
extraction.citeAs: Towards VQA Models That Can Read, Amanpreet Singh et al., 2019
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in a three-stage pipeline: (1) Images were sourced from Open Images v3 dataset, filtered to include only those containing text by running a state-of-the-art OCR model (Rosetta) and selecting categories with high OCR token density. (2) Annotators were asked to provide 1-2 questions per image that require reading text in the image to answer, ensuring questions either directly copy text or require reasoning about it. (3) For each question, 10 ground truth answers were collected from human annotators. Annotators were given instructions to ensure answer quality and were provided with flags to mark invalid questions (e.g., no text in image, not a question, unanswerable).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the Open Images v3 dataset, a large-scale dataset for image classification. The dataset includes images from categories that tend to contain text, such as billboards, traffic signs, and whiteboards. The OCR system used to filter images was Rosetta, a large-scale system for text detection and recognition in images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered to include only those containing text by running the Rosetta OCR system. Annotators were instructed to ensure that answering the question requires reading text in the image, either by directly copying the text or reasoning about it. Questions and answers were collected through a crowd-sourcing pipeline with quality control measures, including flags for invalid questions and hand-crafted questions to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were instructed to provide questions that require reading text in the image to answer, either by directly copying the text or reasoning about it. For each question, 10 ground truth answers were collected from human annotators. Annotators were given instructions similar to those used in the VQA and VizWiz datasets to ensure answer quality. They were also provided with flags to mark invalid questions (e.g., no text in image, not a question, unanswerable).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Crowd-sourcing platform (not explicitly named in the paper)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans. All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions. This indicates high agreement among annotators for the majority of questions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at https://textvqa.org. The paper mentions that the dataset is designed to facilitate progress on the problem of VQA models that can read and reason about text in images, suggesting ongoing maintenance and updates to improve the dataset and address limitations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to address a critical need for visually impaired users who frequently ask questions about reading text in their surroundings. The paper highlights that up to 21% of questions asked by visually impaired users involve reading and reasoning about text in images, making this dataset socially impactful for developing assistive technologies.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases related to the categories of images selected (e.g., billboards, traffic signs, whiteboards) and the types of questions asked (e.g., questions about brands, cities, times). The paper notes that the dataset is designed to study VQA models that can read and reason about text in images, which may not fully represent the diversity of real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to images from the Open Images v3 dataset and categories that tend to contain text. The OCR system used (Rosetta) may fail to detect text that is rotated, unstructured, or partially occluded. Additionally, the dataset may not fully capture the diversity of real-world scenarios where text appears in images. The paper suggests that the gap between human performance and machine performance on the dataset is significant, indicating room for improvement in modeling and OCR systems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is designed to facilitate progress on the problem of VQA models that can read and reason about text in images. It is intended for use in training and evaluating models that require reading and reasoning about text in images to answer questions. The paper suggests that the dataset can be used to benchmark progress along directions complementary to existing VQA datasets like VQA 2.0 and VizWiz.
